title: kbask's observer session is not read-only: it loads the project's and the user's allow rules and the project's hooks
goal: Found by the SP-w6amecjt review: kbask.py remediate and summary start `claude -p --agent kb-observer --permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools ...` in the clone with every settings source loaded, and permissions.allow lists combine across sources and with --allowedTools (kb/public/claude/settings-and-scopes.md:33), so the observer session may run the project's `Bash(python3 _tools/backlog.py *)`, `Bash(python3 _tools/kbgit.py sync *)`, `Bash(git add *)` and the user's `git push`, `git commit`, `git reset --hard` and `sed` rules without a prompt, and the project's SessionStart hooks (intake --file, the coord lease) write into the clone. After the fix, the session kbask starts loads no settings source whose allow rules admit a write (`--setting-sources`, kb/public/claude/settings-and-scopes.md:28, or no Bash tool at all) and no project or local hooks, the kb-observer agent is still the session's agent (passed inline with --agents if a project agent does not load without the project source; confirm flag forms with `claude --help` only, never a paid run), the caps stay, and tools.md and monitoring.md say how the session is kept read-only.

gates.question: How is the kbask observer session kept read-only?
options: --setting-sources with an empty value (no user, project or local settings), --settings disableAllHooks, --strict-mcp-config, --tools Read,Grep,Glob,Bash, and the kb-observer agent passed inline with --agents from its project file
--restricted (ignores the settings files and removes Bash unless --tools names it), no --setting-sources
No Bash tool at all: Read, Grep and Glob only
gates.recommendation: --setting-sources with an empty value (no user, project or local settings), --settings disableAllHooks, --strict-mcp-config, --tools Read,Grep,Glob,Bash, and the kb-observer agent passed inline with --agents from its project file
